M01.reason: A TL-UL response would no longer raise PREADY, so the transfer never completes.

M02.reason: PREADY would be 1 in every cycle that is not a local error or a response, breaking the one-cycle pulse and Access-only rule.

M03.reason: The opcode check is inverted, so a correct opcode gives PSLVERR=1 and a wrong opcode gives none.

M04.reason: o_tlul_a_opcode would be 3'b100 while in reset instead of 0 (and reg_a_rd also differs for the expected-opcode check until the first load).

M05.reason: The local-error branch is inverted: an illegal Setup gives no local PREADY/PSLVERR, and other cycles take the error values.

M06.reason: a_valid is high when the FSM is not in REQ and low during REQ, so the request is not presented or held until accepted.

M07.reason: The IDLE state goes to REQ without a launch and ignores a legal launch, so requests start without a legal Setup or are lost.

M08.reason: Setup is detected only when the FSM is not IDLE, so no Setup is seen from idle and no transfer starts.

M09.reason: d_ready stays 0 after reset release, so no response is accepted and d_ready is not constant 1.

M10.reason: An illegal Setup would not raise PREADY, so the local error is not completed in the first Access cycle.

M11.reason: o_apb_pready would be 1 during reset instead of 0.

M12.reason: o_tlul_a_valid would be 1 during reset instead of 0.

M13.reason: The IDLE FSM goes to DONE when there is no launch and no local error, and an illegal Setup stays in IDLE, so the FSM state diverges from the PREADY completion.

M14.reason: The TL-UL load happens only when not IDLE, so the legal request is never launched from IDLE.

M15.reason: Opcode, address and data would load when there is no launch and hold otherwise, so channel A carries wrong values.

M16.reason: A response completes only when the APB FSM is not BUSY, so orphans give PREADY and real responses are ignored.

M17.reason: An illegal Setup completes with PSLVERR=0 instead of 1.

M18.reason: The default PSLVERR is 1, so PSLVERR is high without PREADY and on successful completions.

M19.reason: o_tlul_d_ready would be 1 during reset instead of 0.

M20.reason: The IDLE state goes to BUSY when there is no launch and stays idle on a real launch, so the APB FSM and the TL-UL request disagree.

M21.reason: The TL-UL FSM in WAIT leaves IDLE only without a response hit, so it stays in WAIT after a response or leaves early, breaking one-request-at-a-time.

M22.reason: The alignment check is inverted, so aligned accesses are treated as errors and misaligned ones are forwarded.

M23.reason: o_apb_pslverr would be 1 during reset without PREADY.

M24.reason: The completion flops are reset when reset is deasserted and operate in reset, so outputs are wrong in both states.

M25.reason: The TL-UL FSM is held in reset when reset is released and runs while reset is asserted, so it is not cleared and transfers do not work.

M26.reason: The strobe check is inverted, so full-strobe writes are errors and partial-strobe writes are forwarded.

M27.reason: The APB FSM is held in reset after release and not cleared in reset, so a transfer in progress is not abandoned.

M28.reason: The payload flops (opcode, address, data) are not cleared in reset and are cleared when running, so channel A values are wrong.

M29.reason: The response condition is negated, so PREADY and the response data are produced when there is no BUSY response and not for a real one.

M30.reason: The REQ state advances when a_ready is low and holds when it is high, so a_valid drops without acceptance and stays after the handshake.

M31.reason: The BUSY state goes to DONE when there is no response and stays on a response, so the FSM disagrees with PREADY.

M32.reason: In REQ a same-cycle response goes to WAIT, and without a response the FSM goes to IDLE, so the same-cycle response case is broken.

M33.reason: a_valid and d_ready are held at 0 after reset release and take run values in reset, so d_ready and a_valid are wrong.
